column2: more realistic cartoon look: light-shaded faces, soft shadows, concrete speckles and stains, brick tones, glass reflections, glowing stack lights, multi-tone grass, rounded shaded trees, corrugated sawtooth roofs, outlined pixel characters, screen vignette
cozy pixel-art look: the whole world drawn at low resolution and scaled up so its pixels match the characters', warm earthy palette with golden light, warm dark outlines, wooden interface panels

full art overhaul mixing a cozy farm look and a rustic one: plank floors, stone-and-timber walls with shelves, tools, notices and lanterns, lamp light pools, cream-and-iron riveted machines on wooden pallets, barn-like buildings with stone footing, boards, dark shingles and a braced door, dirt paths, bushes, stones, flowers and a fence, a day-night cycle with lit windows, plank UI with nails

intro flight over a little town, its industrial zone and into the small factory (skippable); back to one factory that grows in 4 bought stages by level, the meadow and drawn buildings removed from play
messier town in the intro: 1 to 3 houses per lot of mixed sizes, scattered off the grid, roofs both ways, some two-storey, parks, sheds, vegetable patches, picket fences, broken roads and dirt tracks

intro town redrawn as a European old town: a piazza with a fountain, a church with a bell tower and spire, a town hall with a clock tower and arcade, terraced pastel houses along winding cobbled streets (no grid), a river with a stone bridge, the industrial zone beyond

smooth town-to-industry edge (grass fades through worn earth to concrete, houses give way to workshops) and a varied, loosely laid industrial zone: brick factories with sawtooth roofs and smoking chimneys, sheds, silos, a water tower, container stacks, lorry yards, a railway with a goods train; clear ground round the player's factory

countryside round the town and the industrial zone, for a complete landscape: crop fields with furrows and hedges, farms with barns and haystacks, woods, hamlets along country roads that carry the streets on, the river running on both ways

column2: story in five chapters: five ever bigger sites bought by level (wooden shed, brick workshop, works, modern factory, grand plant 16x12) with a flight from the old site to the new and a chapter card; machines move along; the town grows with the company (school, goods station, glass offices, supermarket, stadium, new houses, building sites with cranes); interior floor and walls change with the site

calendar of days and months with time at x1, x3, x8 (day-night follows it); each day machines age and may break, more often at speed: breakdowns repaired with the assembly minigame, machines past their age replaced for part of their price; the next site and the town's new buildings are built over the days and the site can be bought once the level is reached and the works are done

working day of 8 game hours (08:00-16:00 on the clock, factory closed at night); each shift hour every machine has a small chance to break; a warehouse zone of shelves in every site that grows with the chapter (2 to 12 shelves) and is empty after a move; raw bars come out of it, no longer free; an office desk opens the Ufficio panel with stock, orders (+10, +30, fill) delivered by truck after 2 hours and an automatic reorder; a stock chip under the clock
